**Continuous 2.14.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.14.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.14.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.14.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.14.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.14.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.14.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.14.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.14.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.14.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.14.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.14.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.12.1

**A correction about telemetry.** The 2.12.0 and 2.12.1 notes said Continuous collects no telemetry. That was wrong, because two behaviours of the upstream Continue code were inherited: the built-in web search sent its query, with the version, the operating system, a machine id and an embedded key, to a proxy run by the upstream project (docs URLs went there too for sites with `useLocalCrawling: false`), and the terminal agent told the model to add a `Co-Authored-By: Continue` trailer to commits. This release removes both. Web search is off unless you set `CONTINUOUS_WEB_SEARCH_URL`, commit attribution is opt-in, CLI metrics need `CONTINUOUS_OTEL=1`, and the default local path does not contact Continue-operated servers. What is left of Continue-operated hostnames in the code is described under Security and privacy below. [PRIVACY.md](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/PRIVACY.md) lists what is stored, what is sent and what is not.

### Security and privacy

**Continuous no longer contacts Continue-operated servers.** (#627)

- The built-in `search_web` tool and the `@web` provider are gone unless you point them at an endpoint of your own (see Behaviour changes). The proxy is no longer contacted and the key embedded in the code is deleted (it stays in git history; treat it as public).
- The docs crawler's remote path is removed: crawling is always local, from the site you named. `useLocalCrawling` is still accepted in config and ignored.
- CLI OpenTelemetry metrics are opt-in: they need `CONTINUOUS_OTEL=1` and an `OTEL_*` exporter or endpoint, and the service name is `continuous-cli`. `CONTINUE_METRICS_ENABLED` and `CONTINUE_CLI_ENABLE_TELEMETRY` are no longer read.
- A test (`core/egress/egressAllowlist.vitest.ts`) fails when a new hostname appears in source without an entry and a reason in `core/egress/egress-allowlist.json`.
- **No hosted default config.** With no `config.yaml`, the CLI no longer fetches the hosted default configuration that upstream fetched for unconfigured users. It makes no network call and prints where to put a `config.yaml`. (#660)
- The CLI's remaining Continue-operated code is removed: secret sync through the API (`${{ secrets.NAME }}` now resolves only from your environment and local `.env` files, and an unresolved one is named in a local warning), storage sync and `serve --id`, artifact upload, agent status and metadata reporting, the `checks` accept/reject command, and the links that opened continue.dev. `doctor network` no longer defaults to a Continue host (without a URL it prints usage and probes nothing), and the `continue.dev` group is gone from the egress allowlist. (#665)

<!-- pending: #665 -->

- `api.continue.dev` remains in code only as an unused default base (`CONTINUE_API_BASE`, the generated SDK client's default, test literals and a comment); nothing in the CLI calls it for the paths above, and nothing on the default local path fetches it. The hub config-loading code and the SDK client are still present and were not traced to the end. (#665)

<!-- pending: #665 -->

**Commit attribution is opt-in.** The CLI no longer adds `Generated with [Continue]` or `Co-Authored-By: Continue <noreply@continue.dev>` to your commits. Nothing is added unless your own `settings.json` sets `attribution.commit` and/or `attribution.pullRequest` to `true` (project settings are ignored). When on, the default line is `Co-Authored-By: Continuous <noreply@continuous.invalid>`; `attribution.text` overrides it. `CONTINUE_CLI_DISABLE_COMMIT_SIGNATURE` is gone. NOTICE, LICENSE and third-party notices now ship in the VSIX and the CLI package. (#626)

**`PRIVACY.md`** describes what is stored locally, what is sent to your model providers, what is not sent, and how to delete it (`continuous clean`). The README links to it. (#640)

**`continuous serve` is locked down.** The token stays optional on loopback and is required for a non-loopback host. (#631)

- On loopback (the default) the server starts without a token and says so. With a token (`--token` or `CONTINUOUS_SERVE_TOKEN`, 16 characters or more) every request must carry it. With `--host` set to a non-loopback address a token is required: without one the server refuses to start (exit status 2), and a token shorter than 16 characters is refused the same way.
- The token is read only from the `Authorization: Bearer` header; `?token=` is not read (401).
- A Host that does not match is refused with 403 (was 421). Origin is refused unless listed with `--allow-origin` (exact match, no wildcard). A `Sec-Fetch-Site` header other than `none` gets 403 and a request body that is not `application/json` gets 415; clients that send neither (curl, Node, the remote terminal agent) are not affected.
- 1 MB body limit, rate limits per address, and `/state` and `/diff` are masked.
- An approval answered over a tokenless server has no authenticated person behind it and is audited `by: system`; with a token it is `by: person`.

**MCP OAuth hardening.** (#634)

- The issuer is recorded and a callback with a mismatching `iss` is rejected (RFC 9207). A callback with no `iss` is rejected only when the server's metadata advertises `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported`.
- The provider sends its own `state`, which the callback must echo; a callback with an unknown or missing `state` gets 400 without cancelling the waiting sign-in. The redirect URI no longer carries `?state=`.
- The callback listener binds to loopback only. The redirect host stays `localhost`; `redirectHost: 127.0.0.1` is available for providers that need it.
- Static clients are supported with `oauth.clientId` / `oauth.clientSecret` (write the secret as `${{ secrets.NAME }}`); with `clientId` set, dynamic registration is skipped, and registration otherwise sends `application_type: native`.

**`fetch_url_content` and `@url` hardening.** Response size and time caps, a content-type allowlist, http(s) only, `user:pass@` URLs refused, a secret scan of model-chosen URLs, removal of hidden text (HTML comments, zero-width and bidi characters, control characters) from fetched pages, and `requestOptions.headers` / `extraBodyProperties` sent only to the origin of a configured model `apiBase`. (#636)

**Previously unproxied callers now use the shared fetch.** Docs crawlers, favicon and model-list fetches, CLI MCP SSE and streamable-http transports, CLI storage sync, HTTP hooks and the Bedrock credential chain (SSO, STS, web identity) now honour `HTTPS_PROXY`, the OS certificate store and `requestOptions`. Crawls and favicons refuse a redirect to a non-public address one hop at a time. `VERBOSE_FETCH` no longer prints proxy credentials. (#638)

**Hooks.** Hook input is passed through the secret masker for project-origin command hooks and every http hook; `additionalContext` is capped at 10,000 characters per event; `managedHooksOnly: true` in your own settings stops project hook files being read at all. (#633)

**Permissions.** Writes outside the workspace, through symlinks or junctions, to device names, alternate data streams or UNC paths now ask, and reading `~/.continue` or `~/.continuous` is protected, in the IDE and the CLI, including search and glob tools and MCP path arguments (#586, #588, #611). Secret values in environment assignments are masked wherever a command is shown for approval (#591), and the `trustedDomains` in your own config.yaml now reaches the engine, so `ask-unknown-host` fires (#594). More gaps in the large-change, history, infrastructure and dependency rules ask (#603). A permission rule editor confirms a loosening natively (#593).

**Audit.** The audit trail gains an index, a most-asked list and use counts on the Permissions page, a list, inbox and call details in Settings > Permissions (#608, #610), `continuous audit suggest` for rule suggestions (#585), and a shadow reviewer that records what the reviewer would have said, with a spend ledger and Settings controls (#584, #599, #609).

### Behaviour changes that may surprise you

- **Web search is off unless `CONTINUOUS_WEB_SEARCH_URL` is set.** With it unset, `search_web` is not in the tool list and `@web` reports itself unavailable. Set it to a SearXNG-compatible JSON endpoint (`GET <url>?q=..&format=json`, reply `{results:[{title,url,content}]}`); optional `CONTINUOUS_WEB_SEARCH_KEY` is sent as a bearer token to that endpoint only. See `docs/customize/web-search.mdx`. (#627)
- **No config, no fetch.** A first run with no `config.yaml` used to fetch a hosted default configuration; it now makes no connection and an empty local assistant is used until you add a config. (#660)
- **`continuous serve` on a non-loopback host needs a token, and Host, Origin, `Sec-Fetch-Site` and content type are checked.** Scripts that bind to loopback without a token keep working. Scripts that were sent a `?token=` query must move it to the `Authorization: Bearer` header. (#631)
- **Whitespace-only `old_string` is rejected** by the edit tools with an error that names the likely cause (a server that strips whitespace in tool-call arguments, vLLM issue 48753 with Qwen3 parsers) and says how to retry. An empty `old_string` still inserts at the top of a file or creates one. (#641)
- **CRLF files keep CRLF.** A multi-line edit of a CRLF file used to write the new text with bare LF line breaks; it now fits `new_string` to the line endings of the region it replaces. LF files are unchanged. (#654)
- **Plan mode.** The CLI no longer offers `Bash` in Plan mode unless your own `permissions.yaml` sets `plan.allowTerminal: true`. In both the IDE and the CLI, MCP tools (and non-MCP custom http tools) are offered in Plan only if your `permissions.yaml` lists them (`plan.mcpTools`) or trusts the server (`mcpServers: {name: trusted}`) and the tool says read-only; a server's own `readOnlyHint` opens nothing, and a server that came with the open folder never counts. A hidden MCP tool called in CLI Plan is answered "Tool X not found". (#646)
- **Role by tool table.** Each role (chat, agent, background, planner, reviewer, orchestrator) has a fixed set of tool classes; a call outside it is refused at execution with an error naming the role, and unknown tools are usable by agent and background only. (#646)
- **Claude 4.7 and later (also Fable and Mythos) are sent no `temperature`, `top_p` or `top_k`**, on the Anthropic API, the openai-adapters path and both Bedrock paths. `defaultCompletionOptions.omitSampling: true` leaves them out for any model; `false` sends them even to a Claude model that refuses them. Other models are unchanged. (#637)
- **`HTTPS_PROXY` serves https URLs and `HTTP_PROXY` http URLs; https no longer falls back to `HTTP_PROXY`.** One warning is logged if only `HTTP_PROXY` is set. Lower case wins over upper case. (#638)
- **Fetch limits.** `fetch_url_content` stops at 2 MiB (counted after decompression) and a 20 s deadline, and says when it truncated. Limits are `toolPermissions.auto.environment.fetchMaxBytes` / `fetchTimeoutSeconds` in your own config.yaml only. Images, PDFs and other binary content types are refused before the body is read. (#636)
- **Unresolved internal names ask.** A host name that resolves to nothing locally and does not end in a delegated TLD is treated as non-public: the fetch asks, and a redirect to one from a public host is refused. A URL with credentials or a long mixed-case encoded value also asks. (#636)
- **Run limits.** `cn -p` and `cn serve` accept `--max-budget-usd`, `--max-turns`, `--max-duration` (minutes) and `--budget-allow-unpriced`; exit codes 20, 21 and 22. A dollar budget on a model with no price is refused at startup unless `--budget-allow-unpriced`. Interactive chat refuses the flags. (#635)
- **Hooks accept `onFailure` as a synonym of `onError`** (`continue` or `block`, alongside `allow` or `block`). The default is unchanged: a failed or timed-out hook blocks. If both are set the stricter wins; an unknown value blocks. Changing `onFailure` re-asks for trust. (#633)
- **Docs crawler and CLI metrics:** `useLocalCrawling: false` no longer does anything, and metrics are off unless `CONTINUOUS_OTEL=1` (see Security and privacy). (#627)

### Features

- **MCP revision 2026-07-28.** HTTP servers are probed with `server/discover`; a server that offers the revision is spoken to statelessly, anything else uses the classic handshake. `input_required` is retried (8 rounds at most), and `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list` and `prompts/list` are paginated (20 pages, 2000 items; a notice shows at the cap). stdio stays classic. (#642)
- **Plan files from the CLI.** `continuous plan list [--json]` and `continuous plan build <name|path>` for plan files in `.continuous/plans/`; a step's `check:` command runs under the Bash permission decision when the model marks it completed; an in-progress plan is offered at interactive start.
- **Retirement warnings for Anthropic models.** A dismissible chip beside the model picker, one line at `continuous` start-up at most once a day (`continuous dismiss-notice <model>`), and Test connection for Anthropic (`continuous test-connection --provider anthropic`) reads `lifecycle`, `deprecated_at` and `retires_at` from `GET /v1/models`. (#637)
- **Cache-miss explanations** name reasoning or thinking changes, tool choice, added or removed images, and changed tool descriptions or schemas. The Ollama warm window follows `completionOptions.keepAlive` (default 30 min); GPT-5.6+ rows gain 30m and 12h cache write rates. (#630)
- **Hook lifecycle events** now fire: `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Stop`, `Notification`, `PermissionRequest` (a deny answers for you; an allow is not honoured) and `PreCompact`. (#633)
- **Reviewer:** raise-only rules turn a reviewer `allow` into `ask` for `sudo`-style commands, paths outside the workspace and shell startup files, `truncate`/`shred`/`dd of=`, and lockfile edits that add `http://` URLs. An opt-in v3 prompt is selected with `toolPermissions.auto.reviewerPrompt: v3` in your own config.yaml (default off).
- **Tainted-session rule**, off by default: `toolPermissions.auto.environment.taintedSessionRule: ask` makes sink calls ask at every level once untrusted content entered the session. (#647)
- **Accessibility:** polite and assertive live regions (including "Approval needed" announcements), reduced-motion and forced-colours support, named icon buttons; an axe-core gate in the screenshot harness. (#639)
- **Test connection** records probes locally, offers "Turn on recovery", and hints at the API base (#607). A one-line first-run notice in the chat and a once-only CLI banner (#600). The Permissions page has a vocabulary, loading and error states and a first-run overview (#583).
- **First run.** With no `config.yaml` the CLI makes no network call and says to put one at `~/.continuous/config.yaml` or pass `--config <file>` (#660). When a request to a host you did configure fails because the network is unreachable, `continuous -p` names the host and the reason instead of a raw interceptor error, points at `HTTPS_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY`, and with `--format json` returns `code: network_unreachable` (#656).
- **Bedrock:** opt-in prefix repair of broken streamed tool input (#602). **Tool dialects:** Python `True`/`False` for boolean parameters, think blocks in the leak nudge, a Gemma guard (#632); the leak nudge covers every dialect (#601).
- **Stuck detection per agent**, with loop-worker and background-agent identity in the notes (#598, #611).
- **Lab (developer tool):** the lab contract is version 3. Effective n, `--temperature inherit`, per-pass seeds (#644); a whitespace-fidelity probe and server identity in captures (#641); a contract module, result schema and governor (#590).

### Fixes

- **Windows hooks with a quoted command** (a quoted script path containing a space, `"C:\My Hooks\check.cmd" arg`) never ran, because the command reached `cmd.exe` with backslash-escaped quotes. It is now passed verbatim. (#658)
- Edits where the model's `old_string` lost its first-line indentation no longer over-indent later lines of `new_string`. The cause is an upstream vLLM Qwen3 parser bug that strips whitespace from string arguments (vllm-project/vllm#48753). (#641)
- `trustedDomains` from your own config.yaml was always dropped, so `ask-unknown-host` never fired. (#594)
- PowerShell `${env:FOO} = 'x'` no longer asks at every level; `GIT_*` variables are complete (#604).
- Node-only core modules no longer leak into the webview bundle (#651).
- `evaluateRules` complexity that broke core lint on main (#592; no behaviour change).

### Docs

- A docs consistency pass for changes since 2.12.1, with new pages for web search, run limits, plan files, hooks trust and `cn serve`. (#619)
- CI merge-gate branch-protection recipe and failure modes. (#652)
- Research reports, roadmap and decision records (#589, #612 to #618, #620, #621, #623, #624, #628, #629, #648, #649, #653), CI changes (#595, #597, #605) and a worktree bootstrap script: internal, no user-visible change.

### Upgrade notes

- With no `config.yaml`, create `~/.continuous/config.yaml` (or pass `--config`); nothing is fetched for you.
- Run `continuous serve` on a non-loopback host with `--token` or `CONTINUOUS_SERVE_TOKEN`; send the token in the `Authorization: Bearer` header, not in the URL.
- If you used `@web` or `search_web`, set `CONTINUOUS_WEB_SEARCH_URL` to your own SearXNG-compatible endpoint.
- Behind a proxy that you configured through `HTTP_PROXY` only, set `HTTPS_PROXY` as well.
- If a tool relied on `CONTINUE_METRICS_ENABLED` or `CONTINUE_CLI_ENABLE_TELEMETRY`, set `CONTINUOUS_OTEL=1`.
- If you want commits to carry an attribution line, set `attribution.commit: true` in your own `settings.json`.
- If you want `Bash` in CLI Plan mode, set `plan.allowTerminal: true` in your own `permissions.yaml`.
- Claude 4.7+ users who need the sampling parameters sent anyway set `defaultCompletionOptions.omitSampling: false`.

### Known limitations

- The CLI's Edit tool may not be offered to a headless local model in some setups. In one sandbox run with a local qwen model, the model changed a file through PowerShell and not through the Edit tool; the cause was not investigated.
- The provider setup screen still looks up model lists on OpenRouter and Ollama (public third-party GETs) when it opens. This is tracked for a later release; [PRIVACY.md](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/PRIVACY.md) says when it happens.

## Planning

[`plans/ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/plans/ROADMAP.md) records what is built and what is not.

## Not included

The JetBrains plugin and the hosted Continue Hub are not part of Continuous. Hub `uses: owner/name` blocks are not supported; configure models and blocks directly or with local file paths.
